analysis:
Integration review of the reasoning-scoped stop-string change. Changes: per-request stopStringScope threaded through EngineV2Bridge+Submission.swift (new parameter; nil for CBv2NativeBlockEngine, else request scope or model default), EngineV2Bridge+Events.swift (pump forwards the scope to matchedStopSequence for usage metadata), EngineV2Bridge+StopSequence.swift (scoped matching selects the first candidate that alone stops at the same scan), new ReasoningStopScope.swift (think/tool_call and gemma channel spans), MultiModelBatchSchedulerEngine.swift (reasoning prefix computed before submit and passed as scope), docs/changelog/tests, and an mlx-swift-lm submodule bump 2beb401 -> 5ffbb80.

No change touches encryption, attestation, App Attest authorization, coordinator wire contract, cacheScope/cacheSalt derivation, SSD cache storage, KV reservation release or retirement paths. T-041 posture is unchanged. The scope is derived from provider-side reasoningParser and prompt probe, not a consumer-chosen scope. Consumers control only the stop strings, and the scope narrows where they match, so there is no new consumer influence over provider internals, billing or authorization. Reported matchedStopSequence replays the same scope that governed generation.

Residual non-security or unverified items: (1) The submodule pointer bump cannot be inspected here. The engine-side CBv2StopStringScope, StopHoldback and any other mlx-swift-lm changes are unverified, including effects on prefix cache, memory ledger or decoding. (2) Stop matching in an unterminated span, for example a model-emitted stray <think> opener, could suppress stop matching until max_tokens. That is a bounded output-shaping and availability effect, not shown to be a regression. (3) The native MiMo media path passes reasoningPrefix nil, which is a correctness question. (4) The scheduler patch excerpt and head hunk near line 1106 were partly truncated. (5) matchedStopSequence rescans per candidate on the terminal path only, O(candidates x text), and upstream stop-count bounds were not visible.

No qualifying finding. Deeper review is warranted only for the unreviewed submodule bump.
